draft.title: Economic and financial influences
card: Growth, recession, inflation and exchange rates. In growth, incomes rise and people buy more. In a recession, spending falls and sales drop.

Inflation is a general rise in prices over time. It raises a business's costs, such as wages and materials. The exchange rate is the price of one currency in another. A lower Australian dollar makes imported inputs cost more.
Interest rates and how easy it is to borrow. Higher interest rates raise loan repayments for a business and make customers cut back on spending.
When lenders make borrowing hard, a business may be unable to pay for new equipment or stock. Easier borrowing lets it expand.
draft.remember: Economic and financial conditions change both what customers buy and what it costs a business to operate.

a.q: Interest rates rise across Australia. What is a likely effect on a café that has a bank loan?
opts: Its loan repayments rise and customers may spend less
Its loan repayments fall and customers spend more
Its imported coffee beans become cheaper to buy
Its wage costs fall because prices are rising
a.why: Higher interest rates raise repayments on existing loans, and households with loans have less to spend. Lower repayments would only follow a fall in rates, not a rise.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the cost of a loan.

b.q: The Australian dollar falls in value. Mia's Perth shop sells furniture made from imported timber. What is the most likely effect on her business?
opts: Her cost of buying the imported timber rises
Her cost of buying the imported timber falls
Her customers have more income to spend
Her loan repayments fall straight away
b.why: A lower Australian dollar means each unit of foreign currency costs more dollars, so imported inputs cost more. The exchange rate does not change her customers' incomes or her loan repayments directly.
b.clue: A lower dollar buys less from overseas.

a.best: Its loan repayments rise and customers may spend less

b.best: Her cost of buying the imported timber rises

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about what happens to the cost of a loan' points straight at the correct option (repayments rise) and so gives the answer away.
The clue 'A lower dollar buys less from overseas' states the mechanism almost word for word, which gives the answer away.
